# std.task

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Structured concurrency: task scopes own every child they spawn.

## Types

### `CancelReason`

```badger
enum CancelReason { requested, timeout, scope_exited, sibling_failed, sibling_error }
```

Why a task was cancelled.

### `Exit`

```badger

```

### `Task`

```badger
struct Task<S, T> { id: Int, captured: Bool }
```

A child task of scope `S` producing `T`.

#### `Task.cancel`

```badger
fn cancel(self: &Self) -> Unit
```

Request cancellation; observed at the task's next safe point.

#### `Task.join`

```badger
fn join(self: &Self) -> T !{Wait}
```

Wait for the task and return its value (a captured task yields `Exit`).

### `TaskScope`

```badger
struct TaskScope<S> { id: Int }
```

A task scope branded with region `S`; its tasks cannot outlive it.

#### `TaskScope.capture`

```badger
fn capture<T, Eff>(self: &Self, f: fn() -> T !Eff) -> Task<S, Exit<T>> where fn() -> T !Eff: Transfer, T: Transfer
```

Spawn a child whose defects are contained: joining yields `Exit<T>`.

#### `TaskScope.defer`

```badger
fn defer(self: &Self, f: fn() -> Unit) -> Unit
```

Register deterministic cleanup: `f` runs when the scope closes,
after its children have settled, in reverse registration order (also
when the scope fails).

#### `TaskScope.spawn`

```badger
fn spawn<T, Eff>(self: &Self, f: fn() -> T !Eff) -> Task<S, T> where fn() -> T !Eff: Transfer, T: Transfer
```

Spawn a child task. The closure (and its captures) must be transferable.

#### `TaskScope.try_all`

```badger
fn try_all<T, E>(self: &Self, tasks: List<Task<S, Result<T, E>>>) -> Result<List<T>, E> !{Wait}
```

Wait for homogeneous fallible tasks. The first error (in completion
order) cancels and settles the unfinished rest; on success the values
come back in task order.

#### `TaskScope.try_join`

```badger
fn try_join<A, B, E1, E2, E>(self: &Self, a: Task<S, Result<A, E1>>, b: Task<S, Result<B, E2>>) -> Result<(A, B), E> !{Wait} where E: From<E1>, E: From<E2>
```

Wait for two fallible tasks. On the first error (in completion
order), the other task is cancelled and settled before the error is
returned. The errors may differ when `E` converts from both.

## Functions

### `current_id`

```badger
fn current_id() -> Int
```

### `scope`

```badger
fn scope<R, E>(body: for<S: Scope> fn(TaskScope<S>) -> Result<R, E>) -> Result<R, E> !{Wait}
```

Run `body` with a fresh scope. `ok` waits for every child; `err` cancels
and settles them before returning the error. A child defect fails the
scope and propagates to the owning task; so does a failing cleanup, and
when the body was returning an error, the defect keeps it as a note.

### `sleep`

```badger
fn sleep(d: Duration) -> Unit !{Wait}
```

### `timeout`

```badger
fn timeout<T, Eff>(limit: Duration, f: fn() -> T !Eff) -> Result<T, TimedOut> !{Wait} where fn() -> T !Eff: Transfer, T: Transfer
```

Run `f` as a child task; if it has not finished after `limit`, request
its cancellation (observed at its next safe point), wait for its cleanup,
and return `TimedOut`. A defect in `f` still propagates.

### `worker_count`

```badger

```

Number of worker threads (`[runtime] workers` / `badger run --workers`).

### `worker_index`

```badger
fn worker_index() -> Int !{State}
```

between workers when they suspend).
